1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."
Genesio himself, however, admits Marseille's results have fallen well short of the required standard and has revealed he will hold talks with the club's hierarchy during the break.
"It's funny, everyone wishes me good luck. I'm a coach, so obviously I'm linked to the performances and results, especially at a club like OM," he said.
"This is insufficient, I assume my share of responsibility, as others will have to assume it too.
"I'm not there yet, I'm going to digest this defeat, talk to my staff, talk to my directors.
"Because I think – and I'm trying to weigh my words – that it's not normal for OM to be in this situation."
While PSG host Le Mans in their next Ligue 1 game on October 10, Marseille go to Troyes the following day.

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.title: Spalletti relieved to see Juventus banish Sassuolo 'doubts' against Atalanta
1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

Juve have now won three of their first five games of a Serie A season while keeping a clean sheet in each victory for the first time since 2017-18, when they went on to win the Scudetto under Massimiliano Allegri.
And with a three-week international break now on the horizon, Spalletti was relieved to see his team cast aside the negativity of their previous Serie A outing.
He told Sky Sport Italia: "There was a moment when we were forced to defend, then we had to change something and, from there, we got back on track and played on an equal footing in the second half.
"We can certainly get better with the start of our actions and in the build-up. We could have hurt Atalanta more.
"But that's okay, also because the defeat against Sassuolo had created some doubts for us."

Spalletti also reserved particular praise for Randal Kolo Muani, whose performances he criticised last month, despite the Frenchman missing a big one-v-one chance with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.35 – the highest of any shot in the match.
"He had a really good game. I was disappointed when he popped up one-on-one with the goalkeeper because he deserved to score," Spalletti said of Kolo Muani.
"But he was still very happy at the end and we joked about it. We're all happy because now we can recover some of our strong players, who would have been useful to us recently."
While Juve are seventh in the table going into the break with 10 points on the board, Atalanta are four points worse off in 11th.
Sarri – a Scudetto winner in his only season in charge of Juventus in 2019-20 – has now lost nine Serie A matches against the Bianconeri, his joint-most against any club (also Roma).
Though La Dea have now lost three straight games, Sarri insists there is no crisis brewing in Bergamo.
"I don't think so, the first three games were a lower level of performance, but we have been improving," he said.
"This team needs to have more character, to light up that fire in its soul. This is a side with certain capabilities and we need to access them."

480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.title: Greenwood: Man City there to win in Champions League
480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.subtitle: Manchester City return to the Women's Champions League after a season-long absence, and Alex Greenwood is eyeing a deep run.
paragraphs: Alex Greenwood says Manchester City are "going to give it absolutely everything" to try and win the Women's Champions League this season.
City were absent from last season's campaign, but they are back in the competition following their Women's Super League title success in 2025-26.
Andree Jeglertz enjoyed a stellar first season with the team, and they have started their title defence in equally fine form, having won all three of their league games so far.
But their attention now turns to the Champions League, and they will begin their campaign away to Bayern Munich on Tuesday.

City are given the fourth-highest chance of winning the Champions League by the Opta supercomputer, though their 9.1% win probability is significantly lower than outright favourites Barcelona (41.2%).
Greenwood insists City have their eyes on the trophy, though.
"To qualify was massively important; it's an expectation that we have at this football club," Greenwood told UEFA's website.
"But every competition that we play in, we're there to win.

"We know it's going to be a challenge, but it's fantastic for the club. We're going to give it absolutely everything, like we do in every other competition, take it game by game and see how far we can go."
City are facing a German side for the first time in the Champions League.

Bayern, meanwhile, have won seven of their previous 11 matches against English teams in the competition (L4), including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
On their last Champions League appearance in 2024-25, City lost their last two away games, both by a 3-0 scoreline to Barcelona and Chelsea, respectively.
"I've played in this competition enough times to know what it presents and what the challenges are," Greenwood added.
"We worked really hard to get back in this competition where I think we belong. I'm just excited to embrace the challenge.
"Champions League, Women's Super League, whatever competition we're in, we're in it with a real elite mindset to go and win, and that's been our mentality for the last 18 months."

607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.title: Malen withdraws from Netherlands squad through injury
607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.subtitle: Donyell Malen will not get the chance to extend his brilliant start to the season with the Netherlands, with injury ruling him out.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen has withdrawn from the Netherlands' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches.
Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.
It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).
Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.
Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.
The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.

It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).

Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).

Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).

He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.

Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.

The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

          WSL Matchday 3: The Opta Numbers That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Gareth Boyes / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the season, while Arsenal dropped points at home for the second successive match. We use Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
There was no shortage of entertainment across the third matchday of the Women’s Super League, with goals flying in around the league, though Arsenal’s struggles continued in front of goal.

Manchester City maintained their perfect start in a six-goal thriller against Liverpool, Tottenham ran riot with seven against Crystal Palace, while London City Lionesses bounced back from defeat, firing in four goals at Charlton.

Elsewhere, Chelsea made it back-to-back wins, Everton edged past West Ham, and Brighton and Aston Villa shared the points. At the Emirates, Arsenal were frustrated at home once again as Manchester United responded from their difficult start to the season to earn a 1-1 draw.
But, as ever, the scorelines only tell part of the story.
We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout individual performances and numbers that defined Matchday 3.
We’re three games into the new WSL season and Man City are the only side still with a perfect record. But Liverpool made them work for it.
City took the lead before falling 2-1 behind, only to turn the game around and eventually claim a 4-2 victory.
It was just the second time in their WSL history that City have scored first, subsequently trailed and still gone on to win, after their 3-2 victory over Reading in the 2017 Spring Series.
Khadija Shaw continued her flying start to the campaign, becoming the first player to score in each of Manchester City’s opening three matches of a WSL season.
And Liverpool remain one of her favourite opponents.

Alongside Shaw, Lauren Hemp continues to underline her status as one of the WSL’s most devastating attacking talents – and the 26-year-old reached another significant landmark after hitting 100 goal involvements last weekend.
Only Bethany England (69), Vivianne Miedema (67), Beth Mead (60), Nikita Parris (58), Shaw (55) and Fran Kirby (54) have scored in more, while Hemp is now level with Sam Kerr.
And home continues to be a particularly happy place.
Liverpool may have left Manchester empty-handed, but there was another hugely encouraging performance from summer signing Vivien Endemann.

The Germany international is making quite the impression in her first season in England. Three appearances into her WSL career and Gareth Taylor looks like he may have uncovered a real gem for this reshaped Liverpool side.

The Reds pushed City harder than anyone has so far this season, but the league leaders still found a way to win. They have won three from three, scoring 12 goals in the process. Their perfect start rolls on.
Arsenal may have extended their unbeaten run to record-breaking territory against Manchester United, but for the second successive home game, it took late drama just to rescue a point.
After being held to a goalless draw by Crystal Palace on Matchday 2, the Gunners looked set for a first league defeat of the season before finding an equaliser deep into stoppage time.
Nonetheless, that late intervention preserved an impressive record.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

The 33-year-old has picked up where he left off last season, when he enjoyed a career-best 61-goal campaign, finishing as Bundesliga top scorer for the third time in as many years since joining Bayern from Tottenham.

We already knew Kane was one of the best strikers in the world, if not the best – but what we’re seeing now is that he might actually still be getting better, an astonishing possibility for a player who, based on your typical centre-forwards, should be some years past his peak (of course, Kane isn’t your typical centre-forward).

Speaking after his latest landmark achievement, Kane – who amassed 213 goals in 317 Premier League outings for Spurs, placing him behind only Alan Shearer in the competition’s all-time scoring charts – said: “I’m very proud, to be honest, to reach 100 goals in the Bundesliga. Obviously, I’ve done it in the Premier League, so now to have it in a different league is something I’m really proud of. All I can say is a big thanks to the team.”
Kane’s 101 Bundesliga goals have come at a truly prolific average of 1.03 per game. He’s already averaging 0.75 goals per game in the league this season and 0.85 in all competitions.

And none of this should come as any kind of surprise: his overall goals-per-game average for Bayern is 0.98. Were he to score a hat-trick in his side’s first match after the international break, away to local rivals Augsburg, he would pull himself to exactly a goal a game.

It’s little wonder Kane, who has found the net 44 times for club and country this calendar year, is considered one of the frontrunners to win the Ballon d’Or – an individual accolade he’s yet to claim in a career full of them. Oh, and he’s done it at exactly a goal a game.
More goalscoring milestones feel like an inevitability for Kane, who has reportedly been in talks over extending his stay at Bayern, where his current deal expires next summer.

He’s one of 56 players with 100 or more Bundesliga goals to their name – but one of only eight non-Germans. Barring a lengthy injury lay-off or unfathomable loss of form, he’ll almost certainly pass 106-goal Ailton (Brazil) and Stéphane Chapuisat (Switzerland) this term in the ranking of leading foreign Bundesliga scorers – and probably 127-goal Vedad Ibišević (Bosnia and Herzegovina) as well.

Kane can also keep working his way up Bayern’s list of top Bundesliga goalscorers – on which he currently ranks sixth. Next in his sights is Dieter Hoeneß (102 goals), followed by fellow 1980s star Roland Wohlfarth (119).

Another couple of par scoring seasons by his standards and Kane will catch two more Bayern icons: Thomas Müller (150 goals) and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (162). Only the top two goalscorers in Bundesliga history are – unless he keeps playing for Bayern and producing these levels into his 40s – out of his reach: Robert Lewandowski (312) and perhaps the greatest No. 9 of all time, Gerd Müller (365).

It’s also not out of the question that Kane will become Bayern’s second-highest Champions League scorer ever. He currently sits second with 34 goals, nine ahead of Arjen Robben and 23 behind Thomas Müller – and with his goals-per-game average for the club in that competition an expectedly high 0.87 as things stand, he could well surpass Müller by the end of next season if Bayern go even reasonably deep into the knockout stage.
And if contract talks progress as both parties will hope, Kane is bound to keep tearing up the division for a number of years yet.

With a brace in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 hammering of Union Berlin on Friday, Harry Kane has reached 100 Bundesliga goals quicker than any other player in the history of the competition (101, to be precise). And he hasn’t just broken that record; he’s obliterated it.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomSep 20, 2026There was a wide array of displays on show this weekend. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images (De Zerbi), Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty Images (Isak), Marc Atkins/Getty Images (Martínez)The first international break of the season is now upon us and the slate of matches which preceded this natural hiatus certainly had the ‘last day of semester’ feel.

Some unruly classes exchanged goals freely, with five different teams scoring three or more across a flurry of chaotic affairs. Others simply waited for the bell to ring, something almost impressive in the way they managed to expend so much time, energy and sweat without achieving anything noteworthy.
Before focus shifts away from the Premier League for the next three weeks as the fall blur awaits, there was time for one last report card.

Arsenal were battered by the Seagulls. / Clive Rose/Getty ImagesThe tone was set after just 18 seconds. Arsenal were pressed into their own corner from the first throw-in of the contest and never recovered, as Mikel Arteta damningly pointed out after the 3–0 reverse. Brighton converted two crisp long-range strikes to somewhat distort the scoreline, but Arsenal were clearly second best on a brisk afternoon. The fall chill has swept across the south coast and blown away the Gunners’ cloak of invincibility with it. This was a defeat so damaging it sparked questions as to whether future teams could replicate Brighton’s success.
Thank you for your support this evening. pic.twitter.com/AvfnJtH6r5

Oliver Glasner lamented that the “entire City Ground was nervous” and his side didn’t do anything to soothe those qualms. Faced with Coventry’s stubborn block, Nottingham Forest failed to find any moment of inspiration, leaving their manager “frustrated” and “disappointed.” Once the anxiety had surpassed, those were the same emotions shared by the crowd.
Conor pulls one back! pic.twitter.com/PW7TYp0J3f

At this point, Tottenham’s performances are enough to send Roberto De Zerbi into an existential crisis. Not because they are so woefully inept—quite the contrary. Spurs seem to have mastered the art of playing just well enough to get everyone’s hopes up before once again crumbling to defeat.“These players, they don’t need to play better,” the beleaguered Italian boss sighed, the neck of his black T-shirt as loose as Tottenham’s rearguard after he pulled the top over his head to hide from the 3–2 reverse. What Spurs need, according to De Zerbi, is more “blood” and “fight.” Three points would also help.

Chelsea’s defensive woes are by no means new. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesIn Ernest Hemingway’s novel The Sun Also Rises, the character Mike Campbell is asked how he went bankrupt. “Two ways,” he says, “Gradually and then all at once.”Chelsea’s demise at Brentford followed a similar trajectory. There wasn’t anything egregiously wrong with Chelsea’s opening hour on the other side of west London. If anything, the Blues were fulfilling their manager’s demand to be more “boring.” Yet, this suddenly toothless iteration of Xabi Alonso’s evolving side was rapidly condemned to a sound thumping.

ftbpro_01m31f9w4ym4.title: Cole Palmer to ‘Withdraw’ From England Squad
ftbpro_01m31f9w4ym4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott5:30 AM EDTCole Palmer is withdrawing from the England setup. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesChelsea midfielder Cole Palmer is going to have to wait a little longer for his chance to prove himself to England manager Thomas Tuchel.

According to The Athletic, Palmer is due to withdraw from the England roster for this international break. “Load management” is cited as the explanation for a player who has played all but seven minutes of Chelsea’s Premier League campaign so far.

It is a tough call for Palmer, who has not played for England since March 2026 and missed this summer’s World Cup. His impressive form to start the season led to a well-earned recall, and Tuchel admitted he deserved the chance to prove he belongs on the roster full-time, but that opportunity is set to pass him by.
Those inside Chelsea will be disappointed for Palmer on a personal level but, selfishly, there will also be some understandable delight.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

A summer rest worked wonders for Palmer. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesThe vibe around Chelsea is a little low heading into the international break—two defeats and a draw will do that to you—but Palmer’s form has been one of the bright spots of the Xabi Alonso tenure so far.

Four goals and two assists in seven games is a strong return from a player who has openly admitted he has rediscovered his enjoyment on the pitch in Alonso’s fluid forward line. Tactics have played a big part in that, but the impact of a nice, long rest over the summer cannot be overstated.

Palmer spent the majority of last season battling the lingering impact of a groin injury which undoubtedly limited his on-field impact. He racked up just 11 goals and three assists across all competitions and could have few complaints about being left off of England’s World Cup plane.

That heartbreak brought with it an extended summer break. For the first time in months, Palmer actually had the chance to sit down. The focus between May and August was not on matches, but purely on recovery, and the results of that have been clear during the opening weeks of the season.

Chelsea fans wanted to see Palmer back in the England setup, strutting his stuff on the global stage once again, but few will complain about another three-week break for the 24-year-old if it brings the same impact as his last spell away from the pitch.
Palmer has not shown much for England under Thomas Tuchel. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThis is where it gets a little tricky for Palmer.

Tuchel has made no secret of his willingness to keep calling on the same core group of players—those who make a positive impact on the team both on and off the pitch—and clearly values performances for his England side over anything he watches from the stands at club level. We saw it last year with Manchester City’s Phil Foden, who was openly challenged by Tuchel for failing to turn strong performances in training into actual influence in an England shirt.

It means Tuchel’s idea of Palmer is a limited one. Since the boss’s arrival in January 2025, Palmer has played just 158 minutes for England across three appearances, with injuries and poor form both restricting his opportunities at international level. While he has been off of the scene, others have taken the opportunity to build their reputations.

Fortunately for Palmer, Tuchel has proven an openness to change. Palmer played his way into Tuchel’s thoughts this month and would likely to do again if he can keep racking up the goals and assists for Chelsea, but the bar feels like it is going to be a little bit higher for the Blues star after yet another international window away from England.

The attacking midfield spot is not one in which England is struggling. Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham is the headline act, with a supporting cast of Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers in this camp. Phil Foden and Morgan Gibbs-White are waiting in the wings, as are youngsters Josh King and Max Dowman. There is a long queue for minutes and Palmer is slowly falling towards the back of it.

Given there is no major tournament in sight for England, Tuchel is likely to be flexible with his roster selections over the next 12 months. There should be more opportunities for Palmer to impress, but he can ill-afford more absences on the road to Euro 2028.

ftbpro_01m31knbh1sn.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:30 AM EDTA tough day for Man Utd. / Tiego Grenho/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick did his best to remain calm in the face of what Gary Neville described as “the ultimate criticism”—his team simply did not work hard enough against Fulham.

The highs of the first six months of the Carrick era have been forgotten after an ugly start to the current campaign. Only a heavily deflected 89th-minute strike from Matheus Cunha salvaged a 1–1 draw against a Fulham side still searching for their first win of the campaign, with United sitting on just one victory from their first five Premier League games.
Elimination from the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion just days earlier has seriously soured the mood, and Neville did not shy away from questioning the players.

“I’ve never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that,” Neville reflected. “Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team’s energy. Michael has got to stop defending them.
“I get why he’s defending them; he’s loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there’s a long way to go in the season.
“Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No ‘on your toes.’ You should always be on your toes.”
He added: “Very rarely do I say a team doesn’t work hard or is lacking in effort. That’s the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

“I’m always very careful to say that, but in those first 15 minutes of that second half, Man Utd and generally for the first 60 minutes, were a genuine disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball.”

Michael Carrick (left) did not agree with Matheus Cunha (right)’s assessment. / Xinhua/Getty ImagesWhile Neville claimed it to be a lack of effort, goalscorer Cunha argued United simply did not have the energy to match Fulham.

“In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said, backed up by the fact United covered six kilometers less than Fulham across the full game.
Limited energy has been a concern about United’s play all season.
Asked whether he agreed with Cunha’s claims about United’s energy levels, Carrick hit back: “I don’t, particularly.
“The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.

“The response [to Fulham’s goal] was really pleasing ... the way we went about trying to get back into the game. [We] kept the ideas, kept the patience, kept the real purpose to it. We finished on a positive, which is a small step for us ... without ­getting carried away, it’s a good step. We came to take three points but at least we’ve taken something to build on ­moving forward.
“It has been pretty fine ­margins that have flipped it. I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But I’m not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs.”

ftbpro_01m31q0z6037.title: ‘We Had to’—Michael Carrick Provides Marcus Rashford Injury Update
ftbpro_01m31q0z6037.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer7:45 AM EDTMarcus Rashford did not finish the Fulham match. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesMarcus Rashford is considered likely to withdraw from the England squad for the four upcoming international matches over the next 15 days, due to an ongoing hip problem—an absence that may actually facilitate improvement in the longer term.
The Manchester United forward could be followed out of the squad by clubmate Kobbie Mainoo, but is also thought to be carrying an injury following Sunday’s 1–1 draw against Fulham.

Rashford played 77 minutes of the contest, with United falling behind with just over an hour played and rescuing a draw with a late Matheus Cunha equalizer. Manager Michael Carrick confirmed to beIN SPORTS after: “We had to bring [Rashford] off as he had a bit of an issue.”

Carrick also said he wasn’t sure if it was a minor thing the player will quickly get over. He’d appeared to be hurt during the first half at Craven Cottage and was also on the receiving end of a bad tackle from Timothy Castagne in the second half that got the Fulham defender booked.

The Athletic writes that Manchester United have been managing Rashford’s hip since the 2026 World Cup, but it is now expected to rule him out of international duty. In a similar way to Cole Palmer’s withdrawal benefiting Chelsea because of a three-week rest, it could actually be a blessing in disguise for Rashford, who is yet to score or assist since rejoining the Red Devils. The player will be assessed first but is “expected” to withdraw for England.

Mainoo was pulled from the Fulham game after 80 minutes and an injury also makes him “likely” to miss the national team camp. The 21-year-old hasn’t played for England since World Cup warmups in June, having curiously been an unused substitute throughout the whole tournament.

Rashford will not add to his 78 England caps before November. /  Leonardo Fernandez/FIFA/Getty ImagesThree weeks out of the spotlight might help Rashford, who has been the center of attention since the decision was made during the summer that he would reintegrate after spending 18 months on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.
The opportunity to rest, recover and work on his fitness when there has been a background problem that has clearly been bothering him is equally important.

United need Rashford more than ever following the international window. He remains the most recent player at the club to score 30 goals in a single season—and the only player to reach that milestone in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, which came in 2022–23.

Against Fulham, Rashford had more touches in the opponent’s box and more shots than any other player on the pitch. An excellent chance fell to him in the first half in particular, but the effort lacked conviction and that made it an easy save for Bernd Leno.

Carrick at least appears satisfied that Rashford is doing all the right things and heading in the right direction. In theory, once he gets that first break, his confidence should soar.

“Marcus was a threat, he could have had a couple of goals for us,” Carrick reflected on Sunday. “He’s another one who is getting himself in good positions, it’s just not quite falling for him. It will. We know Marcus. We know how to get the best out of him and will continue to do that.”

United’s next match is not until Oct. 10, but they will be heavy favorites against a Tottenham Hotspur team that fell to last place in the Premier League because of Fulham’s draw, is yet to win a league match this season, and has only scored twice in five matches in the division.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.
